name: Glycogen Storage Disease Type I (Von Gierke Disease)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Glycogen Storage Disease Type I

criteria.description: Severe fasting hypoglycemia with blood glucose <50 mg/dL
Persistent lactic acidosis with elevated serum lactate levels
Presence of hepatic adenomas detected by imaging
Deficient glucose-6-phosphatase enzyme activity in liver biopsy
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the G6PC gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe fasting hypoglycemia, deficient glucose-6-phosphatase enzyme activity or pathogenic G6PC mutations, and supportive biochemical abnormalities such as lactic acidosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy is less commonly performed due to availability of genetic testing.

laboratory: Severe fasting hypoglycemia with normal or low insulin
Elevated serum lactate and uric acid
imaging: Hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Detection of hepatic adenomas by MRI or CT
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the G6PC gene encoding glucose-6-phosphatase
other: Deficient glucose-6-phosphatase enzyme activity in liver biopsy
Platelet dysfunction assays showing bleeding tendency

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated liver transaminases without severe lactic acidosis
Episodes triggered by fasting or illness

redFlags: Severe fasting hypoglycemia unresponsive to feeding
Development of hepatic adenomas or hepatocellular carcinoma
references: Rake JP et al. Glycogen storage disease type I: diagnosis, management, clinical course and outcome. Eur J Pediatr. 2002.
Chou JY et al. Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (Glycogen Storage Disease Type I). GeneReviews. 2020.
Chen YT. Glycogen storage diseases. In: Scriver CR et al., editors. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. 2001.
